- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peak values when sentiment is high or trending up.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes; allow for a slight lag in model response to recent highs.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust downward bias by 5–10% in such periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid over-optimistic tail-end forecasts; cap final 5–7 days at 1–2% below true outcome if sentiment is cooling.
- If sentiment is rising sharply, model often overshoots; apply a 1–3% downward correction to forecast peak if sentiment > 0.65.
- If sentiment is falling, model tends to underestimate; add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment < 0.30.
- Avoid forecasting price increases when sentiment is flat or declining; model should show slight downward bias in such cases.
